Local Design Lab · pass 3 · targeted refinement

Denser, bounded, and finally answerable

Journey is a process strip. Attendance holds its width budget whatever the day did. Billing reads as a ledger. The child-grain candidate became Care Team, a real employee-grain Staff card exists, and Health & Safety was redesigned only after its data model was resolved.

Journey shorter 1023 × 119 · was 166

Two summary lines folded into one, and each stage folds its date and outcome onto a single supporting line. The band tightened its rhythm and its glyph. 28% shorter, and nothing about the concept changed — it now reads as a process strip rather than a timeline report.

Attendance overflow bounded projection 0 / 2 / 5 / 8 / 12 movements

Six columns maximum, kept in priority order: check-in, earliest movement, collapsed count, the two most recent movements, current location, check-out. The collapsed count is an affordance — dashed outline, no glyph fill — that opens View day, and the card also states how many are hidden and that the record keeps every one. Nothing silently truncates.

The card does not widen, does not shrink its type, and does not grow taller as the day gets busier. Current location and check-in/out are never the thing that drops.

Billing ledger grammar 1023 × 388

The arithmetic stacks to a ruled Family responsibility total in tabular figures, so how the number was reached is visible without reading. Ledger direction is account balance — a charge increases what is owed (+), a payment, credit, discount or subsidy reduces it (−). This flips the previous signs, which had payments as +. The sign is in the text, so meaning survives without colour. The past-due amount is sized to be read across the room; Pay now is filled and Manage payment steps down to a quiet link.

Staff new · employee-grain 507 × 420

The subject is the staff person. Built as a sibling of Household by construction: the subject's name is the insight, exactly as “Kurzman household” is Household's, the identity row carries presence and contact, and every section is a label-over-value fact grid. Employment carries PersonEmploymentComposition.current; Today reads staff_presence_events; Assignments read schedule_assignments with subject_type = 'staff'.

Deliberately absent

No qualifications or credentials. There is no credential, certification or training store anywhere in Alloy — the only credential table is org_provider_credential_authority, which holds communications Vault refs. Rendering “CPR / First Aid · Current” would have been inventing employment truth to enrich a specimen.

Care Team preserved · reclassified 507 × 422

The previous pass's child-grain candidate, kept intact and renamed. It answers who is caring for this child right now, which is a different question from the employee-grain Staff card — they are not variants of one card. Key care_team; not registered.

Health & Safety redesigned on the data model 507 × 436 · was 569

Grouped by how information is owned, not how it was collected. The critical safety fact leads as the insight in risk red, so it needs no banner and no count. Enrollment health is Business Process requirement satisfaction, not a health fact. Emergency contacts are relationship truth — Household owns them, this card points at them.

Health data architecture — the recommendation

What Alloy stores about a child's health today is two fields: allergy_notes (textarea) and medication_flag (checkbox). Both bind to entity_type: "enrollment", so a child's allergy does not survive their enrollment episode. There is no severity, no reaction, no treatment, and no medication record.

#GapConsequence todaySmallest fix
A1Health fields bind to enrollment, not the childAn allergy does not follow the child across episodesRe-scope field definitions to customer_member; migrate field_values
B1No canonical child-health-fact collection or provider refAllergies, conditions and medications cannot be structured at allOne collection entity with a fact_kind discriminator, plus its collection_provider_ref
C1Document evidence exists only as form_submission_documentsA health document outside a packet cannot be recordedGive documents an owner independent of a submission
D1requirement kind: "document" declared but not authorableHealth document requirements cannot be configuredDepends on C1, then add document to the authorable list
E1None — emergency contacts are correctly owned—Keep projecting, never store

Repeatable structured facts are already expressible. The Forms schema has type: "group" with repeat and collection_binding, and the machinery to land each instance as a canonical record is built and running. Only ONE provider ref is bound anywhere in the repository — "children". The missing capability is a health-fact collection for instances to become, not a new form capability.

Jurisdiction configuration needs no rules engine. A jurisdiction is a different published Business Process revision, and requirements are already per-revision, org-scoped, and conditional on transition keys and field visibility. Oregon's revision requires Oregon's document; another state's requires something else; neither knows the other exists. The one blocker is D1.

Order: A1 first — it is cheap and every later decision inherits the wrong grain otherwise. Then C1 → D1 for configurable health documents, then B1 for the structured facts.
